question: What is the primary purpose of microbial surveillance in healthcare?

options.C: Systematic tracking and analysis of pathogen data
options.D: Direct treatment of acute infectious diseases

explanation: Surveillance focuses on gathering and interpreting data regarding infectious agents rather than direct patient care interventions. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h1)

question: Why is establishing baseline pathogen prevalence important for healthcare institutions?

options.A: It eliminates the need for routine hand hygiene protocols
options.B: It helps distinguish normal endemic levels from emerging outbreaks
options.C: It determines the financial budget for laboratory equipment
options.D: It guarantees complete eradication of hospital-acquired infections

explanation: Knowing the usual baseline allows staff to immediately spot unusual spikes or clusters that signal a developing public health threat. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h1)

question: Which of the following is a primary objective of public health surveillance?

options.A: Providing free medications to all citizens
options.C: Providing timely information for health action
options.D: Conducting clinical drug trials for pharmaceutical firms

explanation: The core goal of surveillance is to gather data that drives prompt public health decisions and interventions. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h2)

question: How do surveillance data directly support national policymakers?

options.A: By regulating the retail pricing of imported surgical supplies
options.B: By determining the architectural design of community clinics
options.C: By setting individual nursing shift rosters in regional hospitals
options.D: By guiding the deployment of immunization campaigns and response teams

explanation: Accurate tracking data informs leaders where resources and interventions are most urgently needed during health crises. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which surveillance type relies on health workers voluntarily submitting reports of diagnosed cases?
explanation: Passive surveillance waits for reports to be sent in by clinicians, making it inexpensive but prone to missed cases. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the main characteristic of sentinel surveillance?

options.A: Checking every single patient admitted to national hospitals
options.B: Using a select network of sites to monitor general trends
options.C: Waiting for patients to report symptoms without laboratory tests
options.D: Focusing exclusively on environmental water and soil samples

explanation: Sentinel systems use designated high-quality reporting sites to represent broader epidemiological patterns efficiently. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of using standardized case definitions in surveillance?

options.A: Ensuring uniform classification of cases across different locations
options.B: Reducing the financial cost of purchasing laboratory reagents
options.C: Speeding up the discharge process for hospitalized patients
options.D: Eliminating the need for patient consent during data collection

explanation: Standard definitions ensure that everyone counts the same clinical picture as a case, making data comparable across regions. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h4)

question: A clinic in a remote area lacks computers but maintains accurate admission and laboratory registers. How do these paper registers serve surveillance?

options.A: They prevent the emergence of new microbial strains
options.B: They act as foundational tools for capturing basic health data
options.C: They automatically transmit digital alerts to the ministry
options.D: They replace the need for national public health policies

explanation: Manual registers are vital baseline records from which data can be manually collated and reported upward in settings lacking digital infrastructure. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h4)

question: Why are bedside nurses considered vital to microbial surveillance?

options.A: They are typically the first to notice unusual symptom clusters or infection spikes
options.B: They hold exclusive authority to declare national epidemic states
options.C: They manufacture all diagnostic test kits used in public hospitals
options.D: They manage the federal health budget for infectious disease control

explanation: Direct and continuous patient contact puts nurses in the best position to spot early signs of emerging infections or outbreaks. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h5)

question: A ward nurse notices that three patients in the same bay developed sudden surgical site purulent discharge within forty-eight hours. What immediate nursing action supports surveillance?

options.A: Prescribing broad-spectrum antibiotics without consulting the medical team
options.B: Discharging all three patients immediately to prevent cross-contamination
options.C: Waiting until the end of the month to include the cases in routine audits
options.D: Documenting the findings and reporting the cluster to the infection control team

explanation: Prompt reporting of clinical clusters allows surveillance systems to investigate and contain potential hospital-acquired outbreaks early. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is the initial step typically taken when surveillance data signals a potential outbreak?

options.A: Verifying the diagnosis and confirming the outbreak
options.B: Holding a press conference to announce a national disaster
options.C: Closing all healthcare facilities in the affected region
options.D: Destroying all historical laboratory records from the unit

explanation: Before launching a full investigation, health teams must verify that reported cases represent a true outbreak rather than a data artifact or diagnostic error. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h6)

question: Why is descriptive epidemiology (time, place, person analysis) crucial during an outbreak investigation?

options.A: It calculates the exact financial cost of treating every patient
options.B: It helps characterize the spread and identify likely sources of transmission
options.C: It determines the individual nurse's liability for the infection
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory confirmation of the pathogen

explanation: Analyzing who is getting sick, where they are, and when symptoms started points investigators toward the source of the outbreak. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge for surveillance in developing healthcare systems?

options.A: Severe workforce shortages of trained public health staff
options.B: Delays in data transmission caused by poor connectivity
options.C: Excessive surplus of advanced diagnostic testing laboratories
options.D: Erratic power supply compromising cold-chain specimen storage

explanation: Developing systems typically suffer from a scarcity, not a surplus, of advanced diagnostic facilities. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h7)

question: How do workforce shortages impact routine surveillance activities in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Data accuracy improves because fewer people handle the records
options.B: Paper registers are instantly replaced by fully automated digital systems
options.C: Staff members automatically receive higher salaries to compensate
options.D: Surveillance tasks become an overburdened add-on, leading to delayed reporting

explanation: When clinical staff are overwhelmed with direct patient care, surveillance reporting often gets delayed or neglected. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h7)
